title: Atrial Flutter Detection System by AdEx Encoded Lead-II ECG
problem: Detecting and quantifying atrial electrical activity during irregular heart rhythms (atrial fibrillation/flutter) is challenging due to signal complexity.
motivation: Need for efficient, deployable systems to detect cardiac arrhythmias, particularly atrial flutter, from ECG signals.
method: FPGA implementation of spiking neuron model using biologically-plausible AdEx (Adaptive Exponential) neuron for ECG encoding. Extracts parameters IFW (Individual Flutter Width) and ACL (Atrial Cycle Length) from encoded spikes for AFL classification.
key_novelty: Application of AdEx spiking neuron model for ECG feature extraction and arrhythmia detection; biologically plausible neural encoding on FPGA.
contributions: Novel AdEx-based ECG encoding for arrhythmia detection
FPGA implementation of spiking neural model

metrics.dataset: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database

limitations: Abstract only; limited to two database records; specificity not reported; no comparison with other neuromorphic or ML approaches; no power consumption data.
